newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may set up more special economic zones.
newsitem.headline: Poland may set up more special economic zones.

text.p: Poland's Economy Ministry will propose to the government by the end of the month a motion which would pave the way for setting up four or five new special economy zones in Poland, the economy minister said.
"By the end of June, the economy ministry will propose to the cabinet a motion on setting up new economic zones in Poland," Wieslaw Kaczmarek told reporters on Wednesday.

Kaczmarek said the criteria for choosing areas for the zones would mainly be their potential to attract investors and said one of the zones would probably be situated near the steel-works in the southern Polish city of Krakow.

Earlier this year the government set up three zones, two in southwestern Legnica and Walbrzych and one in the central city of Lodz. Poland already has existing zones in southeastern Mielec, southern Katowice and northern Suwalki.
Investors in these economic zones are offered income tax relief for 10 years and reduced tax rates for another 10 years.
